message.text:
I have created a place for the new version of the project. The goal is to have a method of estimating the pose of an object given an image from a lidar camera, such as the intel L515. The classical algorithm serves as a benchmark for the neural network, which currently works very well in simulation. The problem, however is with testing it in reality. The network gets confused by the rough background and it is difficult for me to get the same shape as it was trained on in reality. I have thought of collecting background data by just capturing some random backgrounds with the camera and using those with the custom shape superimposed on top and for easier testing, train it with a more varied dataset of 3d models of some desktop items. This project is supposed to be a proof of concept for pose estimation relative to a wind turbine blades, so the shapes I trained it on are similar to those, but it is impossible for me to find objects similar to those in reality. A more varied set of items hopefully means that it will be able to generalize more.
The things that work well in the current setup is the loss structure, the training is somewhat slow for rotation but can almost always find the optimum and the general structure of the network. It fits well in the gpu memory and is very fast at predicting the poses.
Because of those changes and that the codebase is becomming very messy, it needs to be rewritten from scratch, that's why I want to make a new version.
Do you have any more improvements to the current setup? Not in terms of just general configuration changes, adding more layers, but some fundamental ideas that influence the project structure?

I have created a place for the new version of the project. The goal is to have a method of estimating the pose of an object given an image from a lidar camera, such as the intel L515. The classical algorithm serves as a benchmark for the neural network, which currently works very well in simulation. The problem, however is with testing it in reality. The network gets confused by the rough background and it is difficult for me to get the same shape as it was trained on in reality. I have thought of collecting background data by just capturing some random backgrounds with the camera and using those with the custom shape superimposed on top and for easier testing, train it with a more varied dataset of 3d models of some desktop items. This project is supposed to be a proof of concept for pose estimation relative to a wind turbine blades, so the shapes I trained it on are similar to those, but it is impossible for me to find objects similar to those in reality. A more varied set of items hopefully means that it will be able to generalize more.
The things that work well in the current setup is the loss structure, the training is somewhat slow for rotation but can almost always find the optimum and the general structure of the network. It fits well in the gpu memory and is very fast at predicting the poses.
Because of those changes and that the codebase is becomming very messy, it needs to be rewritten from scratch, that's why I want to make a new version.
Do you have any more improvements to the current setup? Not in terms of just general configuration changes, adding more layers, but some fundamental ideas that influence the project structure?

**Proposing modular rewrite architecture**

Providing 10 fundamental architecture ideas for a rewrite with clear modules and interfaces: domain randomization pipeline leveraging compositing real backgrounds and depth noise modeling; self-supervised adaptation using classical estimator pseudo-labels and consistency regularization; segmentation-first modular pipeline to improve robustness; incorporating uncertainty estimation with graceful fallback to classical methods; bridging synthetic-to-real gap via differentiable rendering or style transfer for depth and shape embedding retrieval; object-agnostic pose estimation using keypoints; curriculum learning strategies with staged datasets; comprehensive evaluation harness and rigorous data versioning; per-scene normalization techniques; and maintaining strengths of current hybrid network and loss structures as seen in [positioning/models/hybrid_pose_net.py](positioning/models/hybrid_pose_net.py). The roadmap includes modularizing these components, defining experiment management, and emphasizing reproducibility.

Your direction is good, and your instincts are exactly right: this is mainly a simulation-to-reality and project-architecture problem, not a “make the network deeper” problem.

Given your current strengths in positioning/models/hybrid_pose_net.py, positioning/losses.py, and positioning/estimators/network_estimator.py, these are the highest-impact structural improvements for a clean v2 rewrite:

**1. Split the project into 3 independent products**
1. Data engine (scene generation, domain randomization, real background ingestion)
2. Training engine (model, losses, optimization, checkpoints)
3. Inference engine (runtime estimator, optional refinement, diagnostics)

This prevents dataset experiments from tangling with runtime code and makes your proof-of-concept easier to defend.

**2. Make “sim-to-real” a first-class module, not a side setting**
1. Build a dedicated realism pipeline for depth images:
2. Sensor artifacts: holes, edge fattening, multipath-like noise, quantization, flying pixels
3. Background artifacts: rough geometry, clutter, partial occluders
4. Material artifacts: depth dropout on dark/shiny surfaces
5. Pose artifacts: slight calibration drift and lens distortion residuals

Your idea of capturing real backgrounds and compositing synthetic objects is excellent. Treat it as a formal data source with versioning and metadata, not ad hoc samples.

**3. Add a geometry-aware preprocessor stage before the network**
1. Optional foreground proposal from depth geometry
2. Surface normal and local roughness channels
3. Confidence mask for valid depth regions

Right now the network in positioning/estimators/network_estimator.py sees raw normalized depth; adding geometric priors makes it less sensitive to rough backgrounds and reduces pressure on the model to “discover” basic 3D cues each time.

**4. Train as two tasks: objectness + pose**
1. First head: “is target object present / where likely”
2. Second head: pose only on confident regions/features

This is a major robustness upgrade in real scenes. It avoids forcing a pure pose regressor to solve detection and pose implicitly in one step.

**5. Use teacher-student adaptation with your classical pipeline**
1. Run the classical estimator in positioning/estimators/algorithm_estimator.py on real captures
2. Keep only high-confidence outputs as pseudo-labels
3. Fine-tune the network on these real samples with confidence weighting

This turns your benchmark into a data engine for adaptation, not just a comparator.

**6. Build explicit uncertainty and fallback logic into inference**
1. Predict pose + confidence/uncertainty
2. If uncertainty is high, trigger ICP or classical fallback
3. Return both estimate and trust score

For real deployment this is fundamental. A fast model that knows when it is unsure beats a faster model that is confidently wrong.

**7. Redefine the dataset around “domains,” not just samples**
1. Domain labels: synthetic clean, synthetic randomized, real background composite, real captured
2. Balanced batch sampler across domains
3. Per-domain metrics in validation

This makes generalization measurable and prevents overfitting to whichever generator currently dominates.

**8. Move to protocol-based evaluation, not single loss curves**
1. Pose metrics stratified by clutter level, occlusion level, depth quality
2. Robustness curves: accuracy vs background roughness
3. Failure taxonomy: symmetric flips, translation bias, false lock on clutter

This will reveal whether changes actually improve real-world behavior, not just validation loss.

**9. Introduce shape-family curriculum**
1. Start with broad desktop-like object families for robust geometric priors
2. Then progressively bias training toward blade-like elongated objects
3. Keep a fraction of broad data to prevent specialization collapse

This directly fits your “varied items for generalization” idea while preserving relevance to turbine-blade-like geometry.

**10. Enforce plugin interfaces from day one in v2**
1. Estimator interface: estimate + confidence + debug artifacts
2. Data backend interface: sample scene, sample object, sample background
3. Refinement interface: ICP/post-filter interchangeable
4. Model registry: swap encoders/heads without touching training loop

That keeps v2 clean as it grows and avoids the “messy monolith” problem again.

If you want, I can draft a concrete v2 repository skeleton next (folders, interfaces, experiment config schema, and the minimum viable training/inference flow) so you can start rewriting immediately with clear boundaries.

You are an ASK AGENT — a knowledgeable assistant that answers questions, explains code, and provides information.

Your job: understand the user's question → research the codebase as needed → provide a clear, thorough answer. You are strictly read-only: NEVER modify files or run commands that change state.

<rules>
- NEVER use file editing tools, terminal commands that modify state, or any write operations
- Focus on answering questions, explaining concepts, and providing information
- Use search and read tools to gather context from the codebase when needed
- Provide code examples in your responses when helpful, but do NOT apply them
- Use #tool:vscode/askQuestions to clarify ambiguous questions before researching
- When the user's question is about code, reference specific files and symbols
- If a question would require making changes, explain what changes would be needed but do NOT make them
</rules>

<capabilities>
You can help with:
- **Code explanation**: How does this code work? What does this function do?
- **Architecture questions**: How is the project structured? How do components interact?
- **Debugging guidance**: Why might this error occur? What could cause this behavior?
- **Best practices**: What's the recommended approach for X? How should I structure Y?
- **API and library questions**: How do I use this API? What does this method expect?
- **Codebase navigation**: Where is X defined? Where is Y used?
- **General programming**: Language features, algorithms, design patterns, etc.
</capabilities>

<workflow>
1. **Understand** the question — identify what the user needs to know
2. **Research** the codebase if needed — use search and read tools to find relevant code
3. **Clarify** if the question is ambiguous — use #tool:vscode/askQuestions
4. **Answer** clearly — provide a well-structured response with references to relevant code
</workflow>

"""
Hybrid CNN + point-cloud graph encoder pose estimation network.

Inputs:
    depth_image:   [B, 1, H_pad, W]  - normalized, zero-padded depth image
    model_points:  [B, N, 3]         - normalized canonical model point cloud

Output:
    translation:   [B, 3]
    rotation:      [B, 3, 3]  - valid SO(3) via 6D representation

Architecture:
    depth  → shallow CNN → spatial tokens [B, H'W', C]
    points → DGCNN/PointNet → point tokens [B, N, C]
                 ↓ bidirectional cross-attention ↓
    HybridPool (mean + max + attn) → concat [B, 2C] → MLP → translation + 6D rotation

HybridPool combines three pooling strategies per modality:
    mean  – overall consensus of correspondences
    max   – strongest/most confident correspondence found
    attn  – learnable query weights tokens by importance (suppresses background)
    3C features are projected back to C, keeping downstream dims unchanged.
"""

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F
import math


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Rotation utilities
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def rotation_6d_to_matrix(r6d: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """
    Convert 6D rotation representation to a valid rotation matrix.

    Uses Gram-Schmidt orthonormalization on two predicted vectors, producing
    a representation that is continuous and always yields valid SO(3).
    (Zhou et al. 2019 – "On the Continuity of Rotation Representations")

    Args:
        r6d: [B, 6]  first two columns of the target rotation matrix (not normalized)
    Returns:
        R:   [B, 3, 3]
    """
    a1 = r6d[:, :3]
    a2 = r6d[:, 3:6]

    b1 = F.normalize(a1, dim=-1)
    # Remove component of b1 from a2, then normalise
    b2 = a2 - (b1 * a2).sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True) * b1
    b2 = F.normalize(b2, dim=-1)
    b3 = torch.cross(b1, b2, dim=-1)

    return torch.stack([b1, b2, b3], dim=-1)   # columns → [B, 3, 3]


def matrix_to_rotation_6d(R: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """
    Extract the 6D representation from a rotation matrix (first two columns).

    Args:
        R:   [B, 3, 3]
    Returns:
        r6d: [B, 6]
    """
    return torch.cat([R[:, :, 0], R[:, :, 1]], dim=-1)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Scene encoder – shallow CNN
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class ConvBNReLU(nn.Module):
    """Conv2d → BatchNorm → ReLU."""
    def __init__(self, in_ch: int, out_ch: int, stride: int = 1):
        super().__init__()
        self.conv = nn.Conv2d(in_ch, out_ch, 3, stride=stride, padding=1, bias=False)
        self.bn   = nn.BatchNorm2d(out_ch)

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        return F.relu(self.bn(self.conv(x)))


class ResBlock(nn.Module):
    """Two ConvBNReLU layers with a residual skip connection."""
    def __init__(self, channels: int):
        super().__init__()
        self.body = nn.Sequential(
            ConvBNReLU(channels, channels),
            nn.Conv2d(channels, channels, 3, padding=1, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(channels),
        )

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        return F.relu(x + self.body(x))


class SceneEncoder(nn.Module):
    """
    Shallow CNN encoder for a single-channel depth image.

    Config parameters:
        base_channels: channel count after the stem conv
        num_blocks:    number of stride-2 downsampling stages
        feature_dim:   output token dimension

    Spatial resolution after k stride-2 stages: H / 2^k × W / 2^k
    With num_blocks=3 and 320×256 input: 40×32 = 1280 tokens.
    """
    def __init__(self, base_channels: int = 32, num_blocks: int = 3,
                 feature_dim: int = 128):
        super().__init__()

        self.stem = ConvBNReLU(1, base_channels, stride=1)

        blocks = []
        in_ch = base_channels
        for _ in range(num_blocks):
            out_ch = min(in_ch * 2, feature_dim)
            blocks.append(ConvBNReLU(in_ch, out_ch, stride=2))
            blocks.append(ResBlock(out_ch))
            in_ch = out_ch
        self.blocks = nn.Sequential(*blocks)

        # Project to uniform feature_dim regardless of num_blocks
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(in_ch, feature_dim, kernel_size=1)

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor, return_hw: bool = False):
        # x: [B, 1, H, W]
        x = self.stem(x)
        x = self.blocks(x)
        x = self.proj(x)                     # [B, feature_dim, H', W']
        B, C, H, W = x.shape
        tokens = x.permute(0, 2, 3, 1).reshape(B, H * W, C)   # [B, H'W', C]
        if return_hw:
            return tokens, H, W
        return tokens


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model encoder – DGCNN / PointNet
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _knn_indices(x: torch.Tensor, k: int) -> torch.Tensor:
    """
    Compute batched k-NN indices in feature space.

    Args:
        x: [B, N, C]
        k: number of neighbors per point
    Returns:
        idx: [B, N, k]
    """
    B, N, _ = x.shape
    k = min(k, N)

    # Squared Euclidean distance matrix via ||a-b||^2 = ||a||^2 + ||b||^2 - 2a.b
    xx = (x ** 2).sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)                            # [B, N, 1]
    dist = xx + xx.transpose(1, 2) - 2.0 * torch.bmm(x, x.transpose(1, 2))

    # Smallest distances correspond to nearest neighbours.
    return dist.topk(k=k, dim=-1, largest=False).indices               # [B, N, k]


def _gather_neighbors(x: torch.Tensor, idx: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Gather neighbour features for each point.

    Args:
        x:   [B, N, C]
        idx: [B, N, k]
    Returns:
        neigh: [B, N, k, C]
    """
    B, N, C = x.shape
    k = idx.shape[-1]

    idx_base = torch.arange(B, device=x.device).view(B, 1, 1) * N
    flat_idx = (idx + idx_base).reshape(-1)                            # [B*N*k]
    flat_x = x.reshape(B * N, C)                                        # [B*N, C]

    neigh = flat_x[flat_idx].reshape(B, N, k, C)
    return neigh


def _edge_features(x: torch.Tensor, k: int) -> torch.Tensor:
    """
    Build EdgeConv input tensor from point features.

    h(x_i, x_j) = h([x_i, x_j - x_i]) as in DGCNN.

    Args:
        x: [B, N, C]
        k: number of nearest neighbors
    Returns:
        edges: [B, 2C, N, k]
    """
    idx = _knn_indices(x, k)                                            # [B, N, k]
    neigh = _gather_neighbors(x, idx)                                   # [B, N, k, C]
    center = x.unsqueeze(2).expand_as(neigh)                            # [B, N, k, C]
    edge = torch.cat([center, neigh - center], dim=-1)                  # [B, N, k, 2C]
    return edge.permute(0, 3, 1, 2).contiguous()                        # [B, 2C, N, k]


class EdgeConvBlock(nn.Module):
    """EdgeConv block with dynamic k-NN graph recomputation."""
    def __init__(self, in_channels: int, out_channels: int, k: int):
        super().__init__()
        self.k = k
        self.edge_mlp = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(in_channels * 2, out_channels, kernel_size=1, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(out_channels),
            nn.LeakyReLU(negative_slope=0.2),
        )

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        # x: [B, N, C]
        edge = _edge_features(x, self.k)                                # [B, 2C, N, k]
        feat = self.edge_mlp(edge)                                      # [B, F, N, k]
        feat = feat.max(dim=-1).values                                  # [B, F, N]
        return feat.transpose(1, 2).contiguous()                        # [B, N, F]

class PointNetEncoder(nn.Module):
    """
    PointNet encoder for a canonical model point cloud.

    Applies a shared MLP to each point independently, retaining per-point
    features for cross-attention.  Global feature obtained by max pooling.

    Config parameters:
        mlp_layers:  list of hidden layer widths (e.g. [64, 128])
        feature_dim: projected output per-point dimension
    """
    def __init__(self, mlp_layers=(64, 128), feature_dim: int = 128):
        super().__init__()

        layers = []
        in_ch = 3
        for out_ch in mlp_layers:
            layers += [nn.Linear(in_ch, out_ch), nn.LayerNorm(out_ch), nn.ReLU()]
            in_ch = out_ch
        self.mlp  = nn.Sequential(*layers)
        self.proj = nn.Linear(in_ch, feature_dim)

    def forward(self, points: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        # points: [B, N, 3]
        x = self.mlp(points)    # [B, N, last_mlp_ch]
        return self.proj(x)     # [B, N, feature_dim]  ← per-point tokens


class DGCNNEncoder(nn.Module):
    """
    Dynamic Graph CNN point encoder (Wang et al., TOG 2019).

    This module applies a stack of EdgeConv blocks. At each block, k-NN is
    recomputed in the current feature space, allowing non-local semantic
    grouping in deeper layers.

    Config parameters:
        edge_dims:   output channels for each EdgeConv block
        feature_dim: projected output token dimension
        k:           number of nearest neighbours per point
    """
    def __init__(self, edge_dims=(64, 64, 128, 256),
                 feature_dim: int = 128, k: int = 20):
        super().__init__()

        blocks = []
        in_ch = 3
        for out_ch in edge_dims:
            blocks.append(EdgeConvBlock(in_ch, out_ch, k=k))
            in_ch = out_ch
        self.blocks = nn.ModuleList(blocks)

        total_ch = sum(edge_dims)
        self.proj = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(total_ch, feature_dim),
            nn.LayerNorm(feature_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
        )

    def forward(self, points: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        # points: [B, N, 3]
        x = points
        multi_scale = []
        for block in self.blocks:
            x = block(x)                         # [B, N, C_l]
            multi_scale.append(x)

        x = torch.cat(multi_scale, dim=-1)      # [B, N, sum(edge_dims)]
        return self.proj(x)                     # [B, N, feature_dim]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Bidirectional cross-attention
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class CrossAttentionLayer(nn.Module):
    """
    One bidirectional cross-attention layer.

    Scene tokens attend to model tokens  (scene learns "what in the model
    matches what I see?"), and model tokens attend to scene tokens in the
    same pass.  Both are updated via residual connections.
    """
    def __init__(self, dim: int, num_heads: int, ffn_multiplier: int = 4):
        super().__init__()
        assert dim % num_heads == 0
        self.num_heads = num_heads
        self.head_dim  = dim // num_heads
        self.scale     = self.head_dim ** -0.5

        # Scene → Model attention
        self.norm_s1 = nn.LayerNorm(dim)
        self.norm_m1 = nn.LayerNorm(dim)
        self.q_s     = nn.Linear(dim, dim)
        self.k_m     = nn.Linear(dim, dim)
        self.v_m     = nn.Linear(dim, dim)
        self.out_s   = nn.Linear(dim, dim)

        # Model → Scene attention
        self.norm_m2 = nn.LayerNorm(dim)
        self.norm_s2 = nn.LayerNorm(dim)
        self.q_m     = nn.Linear(dim, dim)
        self.k_s     = nn.Linear(dim, dim)
        self.v_s     = nn.Linear(dim, dim)
        self.out_m   = nn.Linear(dim, dim)

        # Point-wise FFN blocks (standard transformer second half)
        hidden_dim = dim * ffn_multiplier
        self.norm_s_ffn = nn.LayerNorm(dim)
        self.ffn_scene = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, dim),
        )

        self.norm_m_ffn = nn.LayerNorm(dim)
        self.ffn_model = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, dim),
        )

    def _attn(self, q_seq, kv_seq, q_norm, kv_norm,
               q_lin, k_lin, v_lin, out_lin) -> torch.Tensor:
        B, Nq, C = q_seq.shape
        Nk       = kv_seq.shape[1]
        H, D     = self.num_heads, self.head_dim

        q = q_lin(q_norm(q_seq  )).reshape(B, Nq, H, D).transpose(1, 2)
        k = k_lin(kv_norm(kv_seq)).reshape(B, Nk, H, D).transpose(1, 2)
        v = v_lin(kv_norm(kv_seq)).reshape(B, Nk, H, D).transpose(1, 2)

        attn = (q @ k.transpose(-2, -1)) * self.scale   # [B, H, Nq, Nk]
        attn = attn.softmax(dim=-1)
        out  = (attn @ v).transpose(1, 2).reshape(B, Nq, C)
        return out_lin(out)

    def forward(self, scene: torch.Tensor, model: torch.Tensor):
        # scene: [B, Ns, C],  model: [B, Nm, C]
        scene = scene + self._attn(
            scene, model, self.norm_s1, self.norm_m1,
            self.q_s, self.k_m, self.v_m, self.out_s
        )
        scene = scene + self.ffn_scene(self.norm_s_ffn(scene))

        model = model + self._attn(
            model, scene, self.norm_m2, self.norm_s2,
            self.q_m, self.k_s, self.v_s, self.out_m
        )
        model = model + self.ffn_model(self.norm_m_ffn(model))
        return scene, model


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Hybrid pooling  (mean + max + attention → projected back to feature_dim)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class AttentionPool(nn.Module):
    """
    Pools a token sequence [B, N, C] to a single vector [B, C] using a
    learnable query.  The query attends over all tokens to produce a
    weighted sum that focuses on the most informative tokens.
    """
    def __init__(self, dim: int):
        super().__init__()
        self.query = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(1, 1, dim) * 0.02)
        self.scale = dim ** -0.5
        self.k     = nn.Linear(dim, dim, bias=False)
        self.v     = nn.Linear(dim, dim, bias=False)
        self.norm  = nn.LayerNorm(dim)

    def forward(self, tokens: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        # tokens: [B, N, C]
        B   = tokens.shape[0]
        t   = self.norm(tokens)
        q   = self.query.expand(B, -1, -1)              # [B, 1, C]
        k   = self.k(t)                                  # [B, N, C]
        v   = self.v(t)                                  # [B, N, C]
        w   = (q @ k.transpose(-2, -1)) * self.scale    # [B, 1, N]
        w   = w.softmax(dim=-1)
        return (w @ v).squeeze(1)                        # [B, C]


class HybridPool(nn.Module):
    """
    Combines mean pooling, max pooling, and attention pooling.

    Each strategy captures different information:
      mean  – average activation across all tokens (global consensus)
      max   – peak activation over any token      (strongest match)
      attn  – learned weighted sum                (suppresses irrelevant tokens)

    The three C-dim vectors are concatenated → 3C, then projected back to C
    so that downstream layer dimensions stay unchanged.
    """
    def __init__(self, dim: int):
        super().__init__()
        self.attn_pool = AttentionPool(dim)
        self.proj      = nn.Linear(dim * 3, dim)
        self.norm      = nn.LayerNorm(dim)

    def forward(self, tokens: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        # tokens: [B, N, C]
        mean_f = tokens.mean(dim=1)              # [B, C]
        max_f  = tokens.max(dim=1).values        # [B, C]
        attn_f = self.attn_pool(tokens)          # [B, C]
        fused  = torch.cat([mean_f, max_f, attn_f], dim=-1)  # [B, 3C]
        return self.norm(F.gelu(self.proj(fused)))       # [B, C]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Pose head
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class PoseHead(nn.Module):
    """
    MLP that maps fused features to translation and 6D rotation.

    Config parameters:
        in_features:  input dimension (2 × feature_dim after concat)
        hidden_dims:  list of hidden layer widths
        dropout:      dropout probability
    """
    def __init__(self, in_features: int, hidden_dims, dropout: float = 0.3):
        super().__init__()

        def _build_branch(input_dim: int):
            layers = []
            prev = input_dim
            for dim in hidden_dims:
                layers += [nn.Linear(prev, dim), nn.LayerNorm(dim), nn.ReLU(),
                           nn.Dropout(dropout)]
                prev = dim
            return nn.Sequential(*layers), prev

        self.trans_mlp, trans_out_dim = _build_branch(in_features)
        self.rot_mlp, rot_out_dim = _build_branch(in_features)

        self.translation_head = nn.Linear(trans_out_dim, 3)
        self.rotation_head    = nn.Linear(rot_out_dim, 6)

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor):
        trans_feat = self.trans_mlp(x)
        rot_feat = self.rot_mlp(x)
        translation = self.translation_head(trans_feat)                  # [B, 3]
        rotation    = rotation_6d_to_matrix(self.rotation_head(rot_feat))  # [B, 3, 3]
        return translation, rotation


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Full model
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class HybridPoseNet(nn.Module):
    """
    Hybrid CNN + point-cloud graph encoder pose estimation network.

    All tunable hyperparameters live in network_config.json under
    'architecture'.  The network never hard-codes any layer count or width.
    """

    def __init__(self, config: dict):
        super().__init__()
        arch     = config['architecture']
        se_cfg   = arch['scene_encoder']
        me_cfg   = arch['model_encoder']
        ca_cfg   = arch['cross_attention']
        pf_cfg   = arch['post_fusion']
        feat_dim = se_cfg['feature_dim']

        assert me_cfg['feature_dim'] == feat_dim, (
            "scene_encoder.feature_dim and model_encoder.feature_dim must match"
        )

        self.scene_encoder = SceneEncoder(
            base_channels=se_cfg['base_channels'],
            num_blocks=se_cfg['num_blocks'],
            feature_dim=feat_dim,
        )

        # Cache 2D positional encoding for fixed padded input resolution.
        cam_cfg = config.get('camera', {})
        in_h = int(cam_cfg.get('padded_height', cam_cfg.get('resolution', {}).get('height', 256)))
        in_w = int(cam_cfg.get('resolution', {}).get('width', 320))
        num_blocks = int(se_cfg['num_blocks'])

        def _downsample_size(size: int, repeats: int) -> int:
            out = size
            for _ in range(repeats):
                out = (out + 1) // 2  # conv3,stride2,pad1
            return out

        token_h = _downsample_size(in_h, num_blocks)
        token_w = _downsample_size(in_w, num_blocks)
        scene_pos = self._build_2d_sincos_pos_encoding(token_h, token_w, feat_dim)  # [H'*W', C]
        self.register_buffer('scene_pos_2d', scene_pos.unsqueeze(0), persistent=True)  # [1, H'*W', C]

        encoder_type = me_cfg.get('type', 'dgcnn').lower()
        if encoder_type == 'pointnet':
            self.model_encoder = PointNetEncoder(
                mlp_layers=me_cfg.get('mlp_layers', [64, 128]),
                feature_dim=feat_dim,
            )
        elif encoder_type == 'dgcnn':
            self.model_encoder = DGCNNEncoder(
                edge_dims=tuple(me_cfg.get('edge_dims', me_cfg.get('mlp_layers', [64, 128, 256]))),
                feature_dim=feat_dim,
                k=int(me_cfg.get('k', 20)),
            )
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported model_encoder.type: {encoder_type}")
        self.cross_attention = nn.ModuleList([
            CrossAttentionLayer(feat_dim, ca_cfg['num_heads'])
            for _ in range(ca_cfg['num_layers'])
        ])
        self.model_coord_proj = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(3, feat_dim),
            nn.LayerNorm(feat_dim),
        )
        self.scene_pool = HybridPool(feat_dim)
        self.model_pool = HybridPool(feat_dim)
        self.pose_head = PoseHead(
            in_features=feat_dim * 2,   # 2 × C (each pool projects 3C → C)
            hidden_dims=pf_cfg['hidden_dims'],
            dropout=pf_cfg['dropout'],
        )

    @staticmethod
    def _build_2d_sincos_pos_encoding(height: int, width: int, dim: int) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Create flattened 2D sine/cosine encoding with shape [H*W, dim]."""
        y, x = torch.meshgrid(
            torch.linspace(0.0, 1.0, height, dtype=torch.float32),
            torch.linspace(0.0, 1.0, width,  dtype=torch.float32),
            indexing='ij'
        )

        pos_x = x.reshape(-1, 1)  # [H*W, 1]
        pos_y = y.reshape(-1, 1)  # [H*W, 1]

        num_freq = max(dim // 4, 1)
        freq_idx = torch.arange(num_freq, dtype=torch.float32)
        denom = max(num_freq - 1, 1)
        omega = 1.0 / (10000.0 ** (freq_idx / denom))
        omega = omega.unsqueeze(0)  # [1, num_freq]

        phase_x = 2.0 * math.pi * pos_x * omega
        phase_y = 2.0 * math.pi * pos_y * omega

        enc = torch.cat([
            torch.sin(phase_x), torch.cos(phase_x),
            torch.sin(phase_y), torch.cos(phase_y),
        ], dim=-1)  # [H*W, 4*num_freq]

        if enc.shape[-1] < dim:
            enc = F.pad(enc, (0, dim - enc.shape[-1]))
        return enc[:, :dim]

    def forward(self, depth: torch.Tensor,
                model_points: torch.Tensor):
        """
        Args:
            depth:         [B, 1, H_pad, W]  – normalized depth (0–1), padded
            model_points:  [B, N, 3]          – normalized canonical point cloud

        Returns:
            translation:  [B, 3]
            rotation:     [B, 3, 3]  – guaranteed valid SO(3)
        """
        scene_tokens = self.scene_encoder(depth)  # [B, H'W', C]
        model_tokens = self.model_encoder(model_points)   # [B, N,   C]

        # Add positional information before cross-attention.
        scene_pos = self.scene_pos_2d
        if scene_pos.shape[1] != scene_tokens.shape[1]:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Cached scene_pos_2d token count {scene_pos.shape[1]} does not match "
                f"scene token count {scene_tokens.shape[1]}. Check camera resolution/padded_height."
            )
        scene_pos = scene_pos.to(device=scene_tokens.device, dtype=scene_tokens.dtype)
        scene_tokens = scene_tokens + scene_pos

        model_pos = self.model_coord_proj(model_points.to(model_tokens.dtype))
        model_tokens = model_tokens + model_pos

        for layer in self.cross_attention:
            scene_tokens, model_tokens = layer(scene_tokens, model_tokens)

        scene_global = self.scene_pool(scene_tokens)   # [B, C]
        model_global = self.model_pool(model_tokens)   # [B, C]

        fused = torch.cat([scene_global, model_global], dim=-1)  # [B, 2C]
        return self.pose_head(fused)

"""
Classical algorithm-based pose estimator.
Wraps the existing pose_estimation.py implementation.
"""

import numpy as np
import open3d as o3d
from scipy.spatial.transform import Rotation
from typing import Dict, Tuple, Optional
import time

from estimators.base_estimator import PoseEstimator
from pointcloud_utils import depth_image_to_pointcloud


class AlgorithmEstimator(PoseEstimator):
    """
    Classical geometric algorithm using:
    - DBSCAN segmentation
    - PCA-based coarse alignment
    - Two-stage ICP refinement (point-to-point)
    """
    
    def __init__(self, config: Dict):
        """
        Initialize the algorithm-based estimator.
        
        Args:
            config: Algorithm configuration (from algorithm_config.json)
        """
        super().__init__(config)
        
        # Extract camera parameters from config
        self.camera_params = config['camera']
    
    def estimate_pose(
        self,
        depth_image: np.ndarray,
        model_cloud: o3d.geometry.PointCloud,
        seed: Optional[int] = None
    ) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, Dict]:
        """
        Main pose estimation pipeline.
        
        Args:
            depth_image: Input depth image from sensor (HxW array in meters)
            model_cloud: Pre-computed reference model point cloud
            seed: Random seed for reproducibility
            
        Returns:
            transformation: 4x4 transformation matrix (camera to object)
            result_info: Dictionary with detailed results and metrics
        """
        # Set random seeds for reproducibility
        if seed is not None:
            np.random.seed(seed)
            o3d.utility.random.seed(int(seed) & 0x7FFFFFFF)
        
        timing = {}
        
        # Convert depth image to point cloud
        pointcloud = depth_image_to_pointcloud(depth_image, self.camera_params)
        
        # Step 1: Segmentation
        segmented_cloud, seg_info, timing['segmentation'] = self._segment_object(pointcloud)
        
        if segmented_cloud is None:
            return np.eye(4), {
                'success': False,
                'error': 'segmentation_failed',
                'details': seg_info,
                'timing': timing
            }
        
        # Step 2: Coarse alignment
        coarse_transform, candidates, timing['coarse'] = self._estimate_coarse_pose(segmented_cloud, model_cloud)
        
        # Step 3: ICP refinement
        refined_transform, icp_result, timing['icp'] = self._refine_pose_icp(
            segmented_cloud, model_cloud, coarse_transform
        )
        
        # Extract pose information
        R = refined_transform[:3, :3]
        t = refined_transform[:3, 3]
        
        # Convert rotation to Euler angles
        rotation = Rotation.from_matrix(R)
        euler_angles = rotation.as_euler('xyz', degrees=True)
        
        timing['total'] = timing['segmentation'] + timing['coarse'] + timing['icp']
        
        result_info = {
            'success': True,
            'transformation': refined_transform,
            'coarse_transformation': coarse_transform,
            'position': t,
            'orientation_euler': euler_angles,
            'segmentation': seg_info,
            'coarse_candidates': len(candidates),
            'icp_fitness': icp_result.fitness,
            'icp_rmse': icp_result.inlier_rmse,
            'segmented_cloud': segmented_cloud,
            'model_cloud': model_cloud,
            'timing': timing
        }
        
        return refined_transform, result_info
    
    def _segment_object(self, pointcloud):
        """
        Segment the target object from background using clustering and geometric filtering.
        
        Args:
            pointcloud: Open3D PointCloud object
            config: Configuration dictionary with expected object properties
            
        Returns:
            segmented_cloud: PointCloud of the segmented object
            cluster_info: Dictionary with segmentation metadata
        """
        start_time = time.time()
        
        if len(pointcloud.points) == 0:
            return np.eye(4), {"error": "Empty point cloud"}, 0.0
        
        # Get segmentation parameters
        seg_params = self.config.get('segmentation', {})
        cluster_tolerance = seg_params.get('cluster_tolerance', 0.02)  # 2cm
        min_cluster_size = seg_params.get('min_cluster_size', 100)
        max_cluster_size = seg_params.get('max_cluster_size', 50000)
        min_aspect_ratio = seg_params.get('min_aspect_ratio', 3.0)
        expected_length_range = seg_params.get('expected_length_range', [0.3, 2.0])
        
        # Downsample if needed (optional, for speed)
        voxel_size = seg_params.get('voxel_size', 0.005)  # 5mm
        if len(pointcloud.points) > 30000:
            pcd_down = pointcloud.voxel_down_sample(voxel_size)
        else:
            pcd_down = pointcloud
        
        # Clustering using DBSCAN
        labels = np.array(pcd_down.cluster_dbscan(
            eps=cluster_tolerance,
            min_points=10,
            print_progress=False
        ))
        
        max_label = labels.max()
        
        if max_label < 0:
            return np.eye(4), {"error": "No clusters found"}, time.time() - start_time
        
        # Analyze each cluster
        best_cluster = None
        best_score = -1
        cluster_info = []
        
        for i in range(max_label + 1):
            cluster_indices = np.where(labels == i)[0]
            cluster_size = len(cluster_indices)
            
            # Size filter
            if cluster_size < min_cluster_size or cluster_size > max_cluster_size:
                continue
            
            # Extract cluster points
            cluster_pcd = pcd_down.select_by_index(cluster_indices)
            points = np.asarray(cluster_pcd.points)
            
            # Compute oriented bounding box (better for elongated objects)
            try:
                obb = cluster_pcd.get_oriented_bounding_box()
                extent = obb.extent
            except:
                # Fallback to axis-aligned if OBB fails
                bbox = cluster_pcd.get_axis_aligned_bounding_box()
                extent = bbox.get_extent()
            
            # Sort dimensions to get length, width, height
            sorted_dims = np.sort(extent)[::-1]  # Descending order
            length = sorted_dims[0]
            width = sorted_dims[1]
            height = sorted_dims[2]
            
            # Aspect ratio (elongation measure)
            aspect_ratio = length / max(width, 0.001)  # Avoid division by zero
            
            # Distance from camera (assume camera at origin)
            center = np.mean(points, axis=0)
            distance = np.linalg.norm(center)
            
            # Filtering criteria
            length_ok = expected_length_range[0] <= length <= expected_length_range[1]
            aspect_ok = aspect_ratio >= min_aspect_ratio
            
            # Score based on multiple factors
            score = 0
            if length_ok and aspect_ok:
                score = aspect_ratio * cluster_size / (distance + 1.0)
                
                cluster_info.append({
                    'id': i,
                    'size': cluster_size,
                    'length': length,
                    'aspect_ratio': aspect_ratio,
                    'distance': distance,
                    'center': center,
                    'score': score
                })
                
                if score > best_score:
                    best_score = score
                    best_cluster = cluster_pcd
        
        if best_cluster is None:
            return np.eye(4), {
                "error": "No cluster matching criteria",
                "all_clusters": cluster_info
            }, time.time() - start_time
        
        return best_cluster, {
            "clusters": cluster_info,
            "best_score": best_score
        }, time.time() - start_time

    def _ensure_normals(self, pointcloud: o3d.geometry.PointCloud) -> None:
        """
        Ensure point cloud has normals estimated.
        
        Args:
            pointcloud: Open3D PointCloud object (modified in-place)
        """
        if not pointcloud.has_normals():
            pointcloud.estimate_normals(
                search_param=o3d.geometry.KDTreeSearchParamHybrid(radius=0.05, max_nn=30)
            )
    
    def _compute_visibility_ratio(self, pointcloud: o3d.geometry.PointCloud) -> float:
        """
        Compute the ratio of points whose normals face toward the camera (at origin).
        
        Args:
            pointcloud: Open3D PointCloud object with normals
            
        Returns:
            visible_ratio: Fraction of points facing the camera (0.0 to 1.0)
        """
        model_points = np.asarray(pointcloud.points)
        model_normals = np.asarray(pointcloud.normals)
        
        # Vector from model points to camera (at origin)
        to_camera = -model_points
        to_camera_norm = to_camera / (np.linalg.norm(to_camera, axis=1, keepdims=True) + 1e-6)
        
        # Dot product: positive means normal faces camera
        visibility = np.sum(model_normals * to_camera_norm, axis=1)
        visible_ratio = np.mean(visibility > 0)
        
        return visible_ratio

    def _estimate_coarse_pose(self, segmented_cloud, model_cloud):
        """
        Estimate coarse pose using PCA-based axis alignment and multi-hypothesis testing.
        
        Args:
            segmented_cloud: Segmented object point cloud
            model_cloud: Reference model point cloud (centered at origin)
            
        Returns:
            best_transformation: 4x4 transformation matrix
            candidates: List of candidate transformations with scores
            time_elapsed: Time taken in seconds
        """
        start_time = time.time()
        
        if segmented_cloud is None or len(segmented_cloud.points) == 0:
            return np.eye(4), [], 0.0
        
        # Get coarse alignment parameters
        coarse_params = self.config.get('coarse_alignment', {})
        num_rotations = coarse_params.get('num_rotations', 8)  # Rotations around axis
        icp_iterations = coarse_params.get('test_icp_iterations', 3)
        debug = self.config.get('debug', False)
        
        # Compute PCA on segmented cloud to find principal axis
        points_scan = np.asarray(segmented_cloud.points)
        mean_scan = points_scan.mean(axis=0)
        centered_scan = points_scan - mean_scan
        
        # PCA using covariance matrix
        cov_scan = np.cov(centered_scan.T)
        eigenvalues_scan, eigenvectors_scan = np.linalg.eigh(cov_scan)
        
        # Sort by eigenvalue (largest first = principal axis)
        idx = eigenvalues_scan.argsort()[::-1]
        eigenvectors_scan = eigenvectors_scan[:, idx]
        principal_axis_scan = eigenvectors_scan[:, 0]
        secondary_axis_scan = eigenvectors_scan[:, 1]  # For 180° flip testing
        
        # Compute PCA on model cloud
        points_model = np.asarray(model_cloud.points)
        mean_model = points_model.mean(axis=0)
        centered_model = points_model - mean_model
        
        cov_model = np.cov(centered_model.T)
        eigenvalues_model, eigenvectors_model = np.linalg.eigh(cov_model)
        
        idx = eigenvalues_model.argsort()[::-1]
        eigenvectors_model = eigenvectors_model[:, idx]
        principal_axis_model = eigenvectors_model[:, 0]
        
        # Calculate total hypotheses: axis_flips * rotations_around_axis
        total_hypotheses = 2 * num_rotations
        
        # Generate candidate transformations
        candidates = []
        
        # Try both directions of axis alignment (180° flip along length)
        for axis_flip in [1, -1]:
            target_axis = axis_flip * principal_axis_model
            
            # Compute rotation to align axes
            # Find rotation that maps target_axis to principal_axis_scan
            v = np.cross(target_axis, principal_axis_scan)
            s = np.linalg.norm(v)
            c = np.dot(target_axis, principal_axis_scan)
            
            if s < 1e-6:  # Axes already aligned or opposite
                if c > 0:
                    R_axis = np.eye(3)
                else:
                    # 180° rotation around arbitrary perpendicular axis
                    perp = np.array([1, 0, 0]) if abs(target_axis[0]) < 0.9 else np.array([0, 1, 0])
                    perp = perp - np.dot(perp, target_axis) * target_axis
                    perp = perp / np.linalg.norm(perp)
                    R_axis = Rotation.from_rotvec(np.pi * perp).as_matrix()
            else:
                # Rodrigues' rotation formula
                vx = np.array([[0, -v[2], v[1]], [v[2], 0, -v[0]], [-v[1], v[0], 0]])
                R_axis = np.eye(3) + vx + vx @ vx * ((1 - c) / (s * s))
            
            # Test different rotations around the principal axis
            for i in range(num_rotations):
                angle = 2 * np.pi * i / num_rotations
                R_around = Rotation.from_rotvec(angle * principal_axis_scan).as_matrix()
                
                # Combined rotation
                R_total = R_around @ R_axis
                
                # Translation: align centroids
                t = mean_scan - R_total @ mean_model
                
                # Build transformation matrix
                T = np.eye(4)
                T[:3, :3] = R_total
                T[:3, 3] = t
                
                # Quick ICP test to score this hypothesis
                model_transformed = o3d.geometry.PointCloud(model_cloud)
                model_transformed.transform(T)
                
                # Run quick ICP (use point-to-point for speed, no normals needed)
                result = o3d.pipelines.registration.registration_icp(
                    model_transformed,
                    segmented_cloud,
                    max_correspondence_distance=0.05,
                    init=np.eye(4),
                    estimation_method=o3d.pipelines.registration.TransformationEstimationPointToPoint(),
                    criteria=o3d.pipelines.registration.ICPConvergenceCriteria(
                        max_iteration=icp_iterations
                    )
                )
                
                # Enhanced scoring: combine ICP fitness with visibility
                # Check if model normals face toward camera (at origin)
                self._ensure_normals(model_transformed)
                visible_ratio_test = self._compute_visibility_ratio(model_transformed)
                
                # Combined score: ICP fitness weighted by visibility^2
                score = result.fitness * (visible_ratio_test ** 2)
                
                candidates.append({
                    'transformation': T @ result.transformation,
                    'score': score,
                    'fitness': result.fitness,
                    'rmse': result.inlier_rmse,
                    'visible_ratio': visible_ratio_test
                })
        
        # Sort by score (descending)
        candidates.sort(key=lambda x: x['score'], reverse=True)
        
        if debug:
            print(f"  [Coarse] Testing {total_hypotheses} hypotheses")
            print(f"  [Coarse] Best: fitness={candidates[0]['fitness']:.3f}, visible={candidates[0]['visible_ratio']:.2f}")
            print(f"  [Coarse] Top 3:")
            for i in range(min(3, len(candidates))):
                c = candidates[i]
                print(f"    [{i}] score={c['score']:.4f}, fitness={c['fitness']:.3f}, visible={c['visible_ratio']:.2f}")
            
            # Check initial coarse alignment fitness directly
            model_at_coarse = o3d.geometry.PointCloud(model_cloud)
            model_at_coarse.transform(candidates[0]['transformation'])
            
            # Compute overlap with segmented cloud
            dists = model_at_coarse.compute_point_cloud_distance(segmented_cloud)
            inliers = np.sum(np.asarray(dists) < 0.05)
            direct_fitness = inliers / len(model_at_coarse.points)
            print(f"  [Coarse] Direct fitness check: {direct_fitness:.3f} ({inliers}/{len(model_at_coarse.points)} points)")
        
        return candidates[0]['transformation'], candidates, time.time() - start_time


    def _refine_pose_icp(self, segmented_cloud, model_cloud, initial_transform):
        """
        Refine pose estimate using two-stage point-to-point ICP.
        
        Args:
            segmented_cloud: Segmented object point cloud
            model_cloud: Reference model point cloud
            initial_transform: Initial 4x4 transformation matrix
            
        Returns:
            refined_transform: Refined 4x4 transformation matrix
            registration_result: ICP result object with fitness metrics
            time_elapsed: Time taken in seconds
        """
        start_time = time.time()
        
        # Get ICP parameters
        icp_params = self.config.get('icp_refinement', {})
        max_iterations = icp_params.get('max_iterations', 30)
        max_correspondence_dist = icp_params.get('max_correspondence_distance', 0.02)
        relative_fitness = icp_params.get('relative_fitness', 1e-6)
        relative_rmse = icp_params.get('relative_rmse', 1e-6)
        debug = self.config.get('debug', False)
        
        # Make copies if normals need to be estimated to avoid modifying input arguments
        if not segmented_cloud.has_normals():
            segmented_cloud = o3d.geometry.PointCloud(segmented_cloud)
            segmented_cloud.estimate_normals(
                search_param=o3d.geometry.KDTreeSearchParamHybrid(radius=0.05, max_nn=30)
            )
        
        if not model_cloud.has_normals():
            model_cloud = o3d.geometry.PointCloud(model_cloud)
            model_cloud.estimate_normals(
                search_param=o3d.geometry.KDTreeSearchParamHybrid(radius=0.05, max_nn=30)
            )
        
        
        # Two-stage ICP: point-to-point first for robustness, then point-to-plane for accuracy
        if debug:
            print(f"  [ICP] Stage 1: Point-to-Point (robust, 2x distance)")
        
        result_p2p = o3d.pipelines.registration.registration_icp(
            model_cloud,
            segmented_cloud,
            max_correspondence_dist * 2,
            initial_transform,
            o3d.pipelines.registration.TransformationEstimationPointToPoint(),
            o3d.pipelines.registration.ICPConvergenceCriteria(
                relative_fitness=relative_fitness,
                relative_rmse=relative_rmse,
                max_iteration=20
            )
        )
        
        if debug:
            print(f"    fitness={result_p2p.fitness:.3f}, RMSE={result_p2p.inlier_rmse:.4f}m")
            print(f"  [ICP] Stage 2: Point-to-Point (tighter distance)")
        
        result = o3d.pipelines.registration.registration_icp(
            model_cloud,
            segmented_cloud,
            max_correspondence_dist,
            result_p2p.transformation,
            o3d.pipelines.registration.TransformationEstimationPointToPoint(),
            o3d.pipelines.registration.ICPConvergenceCriteria(
                relative_fitness=relative_fitness,
                relative_rmse=relative_rmse,
                max_iteration=max_iterations - 20
            )
        )
        
        if debug:
            print(f"    fitness={result.fitness:.3f}, RMSE={result.inlier_rmse:.4f}m")
        
        # Validate visibility and test flip corrections to prevent opposite-side convergence
        T_refined = result.transformation
        model_check = o3d.geometry.PointCloud(model_cloud)
        model_check.transform(T_refined)
        
        self._ensure_normals(model_check)
        visible_ratio = self._compute_visibility_ratio(model_check)
        
        if debug:
            print(f"  [ICP] Visibility: {visible_ratio:.1%} faces camera")
        
        # Get model's principal axes for flip correction testing
        model_center = model_check.get_center()
        model_points = np.asarray(model_check.points)
        points_centered = model_points - model_center
        cov = np.cov(points_centered.T)
        eigenvalues, eigenvectors = np.linalg.eigh(cov)
        idx = eigenvalues.argsort()[::-1]
        eigenvectors = eigenvectors[:, idx]
        
        correction_candidates = []
        
        # Test 180° flip around each perpendicular axis
        for axis_idx in [1, 2]:
            flip_axis = eigenvectors[:, axis_idx]
            R_flip = Rotation.from_rotvec(np.pi * flip_axis).as_matrix()
            
            # Apply flip around model center
            T_flip = np.eye(4)
            T_flip[:3, :3] = R_flip
            T_flip[:3, 3] = model_center - R_flip @ model_center
            
            T_corrected = T_flip @ T_refined
            
            # Test with quick ICP (fewer iterations for speed)
            result_corrected = o3d.pipelines.registration.registration_icp(
                model_cloud,
                segmented_cloud,
                max_correspondence_dist,
                T_corrected,
                o3d.pipelines.registration.TransformationEstimationPointToPlane(),
                o3d.pipelines.registration.ICPConvergenceCriteria(
                    relative_fitness=relative_fitness,
                    relative_rmse=relative_rmse,
                    max_iteration=10
                )
            )
            
            # Check visibility of corrected pose
            model_corrected = o3d.geometry.PointCloud(model_cloud)
            model_corrected.transform(result_corrected.transformation)
            
            self._ensure_normals(model_corrected)
            visible_ratio_corr = self._compute_visibility_ratio(model_corrected)
            
            # Strong visibility weighting
            score = result_corrected.fitness * (visible_ratio_corr ** 4)
            
            correction_candidates.append({
                'transformation': result_corrected.transformation,
                'fitness': result_corrected.fitness,
                'visible_ratio': visible_ratio_corr,
                'score': score,
                'axis': axis_idx
            })
        
        # Add original as candidate
        correction_candidates.append({
            'transformation': T_refined,
            'fitness': result.fitness,
            'visible_ratio': visible_ratio,
            'score': result.fitness * (visible_ratio ** 4),
            'axis': -1
        })
        
        # Pick best candidate
        best_correction = max(correction_candidates, key=lambda x: x['score'])
        
        if debug:
            print(f"  [ICP] Flip correction candidates:")
            for i, c in enumerate(correction_candidates):
                label = f"axis={c['axis']}" if c['axis'] != -1 else "original"
                print(f"    [{label}] fitness={c['fitness']:.3f}, visible={c['visible_ratio']:.1%}, score={c['score']:.4f}")
            if best_correction['axis'] != -1:
                print(f"  [ICP] Applied flip correction: axis={best_correction['axis']}")
            else:
                print(f"  [ICP] Kept original pose")
        
        if best_correction['axis'] != -1:
            return best_correction['transformation'], result, time.time() - start_time
        
        return T_refined, result, time.time() - start_time

"""
Neural network-based pose estimator.

Loads HybridPoseNet from a checkpoint and runs single-sample inference.
Preprocessing mirrors dataset.py so that training and inference distributions match.
"""

import time
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Dict, Optional, Tuple

import numpy as np
import open3d as o3d

from estimators.base_estimator import PoseEstimator
from pointcloud_utils import depth_image_to_pointcloud


class NetworkEstimator(PoseEstimator):
    """
    HybridPoseNet-based pose estimator.

    The model is loaded lazily on the first call to estimate_pose() so that
    importing this class is always safe even when no checkpoint exists yet.
    """

    def __init__(self, config: Dict):
        """
        Args:
            config: Contents of network_config.json
        """
        super().__init__(config)

        inference  = config.get('inference', {})
        cam        = config['camera']
        data_cfg   = config.get('data', {})

        self.checkpoint_path = inference.get('checkpoint', 'checkpoints/best.pth')
        self.device_str      = inference.get('device', 'cpu')
        self.use_icp_refinement = inference.get('use_icp_refinement', False)

        icp_cfg = inference.get('icp_refinement', {})
        self.icp_max_iterations = int(icp_cfg.get('max_iterations', 30))
        self.icp_max_correspondence_distance = float(
            icp_cfg.get('max_correspondence_distance', 0.02)
        )
        self.icp_relative_fitness = float(icp_cfg.get('relative_fitness', 1e-6))
        self.icp_relative_rmse = float(icp_cfg.get('relative_rmse', 1e-6))

        self.camera_params = cam
        self.depth_max     = cam['depth_range']['max']
        self.img_height    = cam['resolution']['height']
        self.img_width     = cam['resolution']['width']
        self.padded_height = cam.get('padded_height', self.img_height)
        self.pad_rows      = self.padded_height - self.img_height
        self.num_points    = data_cfg.get('num_points', 512)

        self._torch_model = None   # loaded lazily

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Lazy model loading
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _load_model(self):
        """Load checkpoint and set model to eval mode."""
        if self._torch_model is not None:
            return

        import torch
        from models.hybrid_pose_net import HybridPoseNet

        device = torch.device(self.device_str)

        ckpt_path = Path(self.checkpoint_path)
        if not ckpt_path.exists():
            raise FileNotFoundError(
                f"[{self.name}] Checkpoint not found: {ckpt_path}\n"
                "Run train.py first to produce a checkpoint."
            )

        ckpt  = torch.load(ckpt_path, map_location=device)
        # The checkpoint stores the full config so the arch is always synced
        model = HybridPoseNet(ckpt['config'])
        model.load_state_dict(ckpt['state_dict'])
        model.to(device)
        model.eval()

        self._torch_model = model
        self._device      = device
        print(f"[{self.name}] Loaded checkpoint '{ckpt_path}' "
              f"(epoch {ckpt.get('epoch','?')}, "
              f"val_loss={ckpt.get('val_loss', float('nan')):.4f})")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Preprocessing
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _preprocess_depth(self, depth_image: np.ndarray) -> 'torch.Tensor':
        """Normalize + pad depth to expected tensor shape [1, 1, H_pad, W]."""
        import torch
        depth = np.clip(depth_image / self.depth_max, 0.0, 1.0).astype(np.float32)
        if self.pad_rows > 0:
            depth = np.pad(depth, ((0, self.pad_rows), (0, 0)))
        return torch.from_numpy(depth).unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(0)   # [1,1,H_pad,W]

    def _preprocess_model_points(self,
                                 model_cloud: o3d.geometry.PointCloud,
                                 seed: Optional[int]) -> Tuple['torch.Tensor', float]:
        """
        Subsample to num_points, normalize to unit sphere.
        Returns tensor [1, num_points, 3] and the scale factor used.
        """
        import torch
        pts = np.asarray(model_cloud.points, dtype=np.float32)
        N   = len(pts)

        rng = np.random.default_rng(seed if seed is not None else 0)
        if N >= self.num_points:
            idx = rng.choice(N, self.num_points, replace=False)
        else:
            idx = rng.choice(N, self.num_points, replace=True)
        pts = pts[idx]

        scale = float(np.abs(pts).max()) + 1e-8
        pts   = (pts / scale).astype(np.float32)

        return torch.from_numpy(pts).unsqueeze(0), scale   # [1,N,3], scalar

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Inference
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _refine_pose_icp(
        self,
        depth_image: np.ndarray,
        model_cloud: o3d.geometry.PointCloud,
        initial_transform: np.ndarray,
    ) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, Dict, float]:
        """Refine NN pose with two-stage point-to-point ICP."""
        start_time = time.time()

        scene_cloud = depth_image_to_pointcloud(depth_image, self.camera_params)
        if len(scene_cloud.points) == 0:
            return initial_transform, {
                'applied': False,
                'error': 'empty_scene_pointcloud',
                'fitness': 0.0,
                'rmse': float('inf'),
            }, time.time() - start_time

        max_iter = max(self.icp_max_iterations, 1)
        stage1_iter = min(20, max_iter)
        stage2_iter = max(max_iter - stage1_iter, 1)

        try:
            result_p2p_1 = o3d.pipelines.registration.registration_icp(
                model_cloud,
                scene_cloud,
                self.icp_max_correspondence_distance * 2.0,
                initial_transform,
                o3d.pipelines.registration.TransformationEstimationPointToPoint(),
                o3d.pipelines.registration.ICPConvergenceCriteria(
                    relative_fitness=self.icp_relative_fitness,
                    relative_rmse=self.icp_relative_rmse,
                    max_iteration=stage1_iter,
                ),
            )

            result_p2p_2 = o3d.pipelines.registration.registration_icp(
                model_cloud,
                scene_cloud,
                self.icp_max_correspondence_distance,
                result_p2p_1.transformation,
                o3d.pipelines.registration.TransformationEstimationPointToPoint(),
                o3d.pipelines.registration.ICPConvergenceCriteria(
                    relative_fitness=self.icp_relative_fitness,
                    relative_rmse=self.icp_relative_rmse,
                    max_iteration=stage2_iter,
                ),
            )

            return result_p2p_2.transformation, {
                'applied': True,
                'fitness': float(result_p2p_2.fitness),
                'rmse': float(result_p2p_2.inlier_rmse),
                'iterations_stage1': stage1_iter,
                'iterations_stage2': stage2_iter,
            }, time.time() - start_time
        except Exception as exc:
            return initial_transform, {
                'applied': False,
                'error': f'icp_failed: {exc}',
                'fitness': 0.0,
                'rmse': float('inf'),
            }, time.time() - start_time

    def estimate_pose(
        self,
        depth_image: np.ndarray,
        model_cloud: o3d.geometry.PointCloud,
        seed: Optional[int] = None,
    ) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, Dict]:
        """
        Estimate pose using HybridPoseNet.

        Args:
            depth_image: [H, W] float32 depth array in metres
            model_cloud: Open3D PointCloud of the canonical model
            seed:        Optional random seed for point subsampling

        Returns:
            transformation: [4, 4] float64 homogeneous transform (camera ← model)
            result_info:    dict matching AlgorithmEstimator format
        """
        start_time = time.time()
        timing = {}

        t_load_start = time.time()
        self._load_model()   # no-op if already loaded
        timing['model_load'] = time.time() - t_load_start

        import torch
        from scipy.spatial.transform import Rotation

        with torch.no_grad():
            # Preprocess depth (CPU)
            t_depth_pre_start = time.time()
            depth_t_cpu = self._preprocess_depth(depth_image)
            timing['preprocess_depth'] = time.time() - t_depth_pre_start

            # Preprocess model points (CPU)
            t_model_pre_start = time.time()
            pts_t_cpu, _ = self._preprocess_model_points(model_cloud, seed)
            timing['preprocess_model_points'] = time.time() - t_model_pre_start

            # Host-to-device transfer
            t_transfer_start = time.time()
            depth_t = depth_t_cpu.to(self._device)
            pts_t = pts_t_cpu.to(self._device)
            timing['to_device'] = time.time() - t_transfer_start

            # Network forward pass
            t_forward_start = time.time()
            pred_t, pred_R = self._torch_model(depth_t, pts_t)  # [1,3], [1,3,3]

            # Ensure accurate CUDA timing for forward segment
            if self._device.type == 'cuda':
                torch.cuda.synchronize(self._device)
            timing['forward_pass'] = time.time() - t_forward_start

        # Device-to-host transfer
        t_d2h_start = time.time()
        pred_t = pred_t[0].cpu().numpy()          # [3]
        pred_R = pred_R[0].cpu().numpy()          # [3,3]
        timing['to_cpu'] = time.time() - t_d2h_start

        # Assemble 4×4 transform
        t_post_start = time.time()
        transform        = np.eye(4, dtype=np.float64)
        transform[:3, :3] = pred_R
        transform[:3, 3]  = pred_t
        timing['postprocess_transform'] = time.time() - t_post_start

        icp_info = {
            'applied': False,
            'fitness': None,
            'rmse': None,
        }
        timing['inference'] = (
            timing['preprocess_depth']
            + timing['preprocess_model_points']
            + timing['to_device']
            + timing['forward_pass']
            + timing['to_cpu']
            + timing['postprocess_transform']
        )

        if self.use_icp_refinement:
            transform, icp_info, timing['icp'] = self._refine_pose_icp(
                depth_image=depth_image,
                model_cloud=model_cloud,
                initial_transform=transform,
            )
            pred_R = transform[:3, :3]
            pred_t = transform[:3, 3]

        euler_angles = Rotation.from_matrix(pred_R).as_euler('xyz', degrees=True)
        elapsed      = time.time() - start_time
        timing['total'] = elapsed

        result_info = {
            'success':         True,
            'transformation':  transform,
            'position':        pred_t,
            'orientation_euler': euler_angles,
            'timing':          timing,
            'estimator_name':  self.name,
            'model_cloud':     model_cloud,
            'icp_refinement':  icp_info,
        }
        return transform, result_info

            timing['to_device'] = time.time() - t_transfer_start

            # Network forward pass
            t_forward_start = time.time()
            pred_t, pred_R = self._torch_model(depth_t, pts_t)  # [1,3], [1,3,3]

            # Ensure accurate CUDA timing for forward segment
            if self._device.type == 'cuda':
                torch.cuda.synchronize(self._device)
            timing['forward_pass'] = time.time() - t_forward_start

        # Device-to-host transfer
        t_d2h_start = time.time()
        pred_t = pred_t[0].cpu().numpy()          # [3]
        pred_R = pred_R[0].cpu().numpy()          # [3,3]
        timing['to_cpu'] = time.time() - t_d2h_start

        # Assemble 4×4 transform
        t_post_start = time.time()
        transform        = np.eye(4, dtype=np.float64)
        transform[:3, :3] = pred_R
        transform[:3, 3]  = pred_t
        timing['postprocess_transform'] = time.time() - t_post_start

        icp_info = {
            'applied': False,
            'fitness': None,
            'rmse': None,
        }
        timing['inference'] = (
            timing['preprocess_depth']
            + timing['preprocess_model_points']
            + timing['to_device']
            + timing['forward_pass']
            + timing['to_cpu']
            + timing['postprocess_transform']
        )

        if self.use_icp_refinement:
            transform, icp_info, timing['icp'] = self._refine_pose_icp(
                depth_image=depth_image,
                model_cloud=model_cloud,
                initial_transform=transform,
            )
            pred_R = transform[:3, :3]
            pred_t = transform[:3, 3]

        euler_angles = Rotation.from_matrix(pred_R).as_euler('xyz', degrees=True)
        elapsed      = time.time() - start_time
        timing['total'] = elapsed

        result_info = {
            'success':         True,
            'transformation':  transform,
            'position':        pred_t,
            'orientation_euler': euler_angles,
            'timing':          timing,
            'estimator_name':  self.name,
            'model_cloud':     model_cloud,
            'icp_refinement':  icp_info,
        }
        return transform, result_info

Your direction is good, and your instincts are exactly right: this is mainly a simulation-to-reality and project-architecture problem, not a “make the network deeper” problem.

Given your current strengths in [positioning/models/hybrid_pose_net.py](positioning/models/hybrid_pose_net.py), [positioning/losses.py](positioning/losses.py), and [positioning/estimators/network_estimator.py](positioning/estimators/network_estimator.py), these are the highest-impact structural improvements for a clean v2 rewrite:

**1. Split the project into 3 independent products**
1. Data engine (scene generation, domain randomization, real background ingestion)
2. Training engine (model, losses, optimization, checkpoints)
3. Inference engine (runtime estimator, optional refinement, diagnostics)

This prevents dataset experiments from tangling with runtime code and makes your proof-of-concept easier to defend.

**2. Make “sim-to-real” a first-class module, not a side setting**
1. Build a dedicated realism pipeline for depth images:
2. Sensor artifacts: holes, edge fattening, multipath-like noise, quantization, flying pixels
3. Background artifacts: rough geometry, clutter, partial occluders
4. Material artifacts: depth dropout on dark/shiny surfaces
5. Pose artifacts: slight calibration drift and lens distortion residuals

Your idea of capturing real backgrounds and compositing synthetic objects is excellent. Treat it as a formal data source with versioning and metadata, not ad hoc samples.

**3. Add a geometry-aware preprocessor stage before the network**
1. Optional foreground proposal from depth geometry
2. Surface normal and local roughness channels
3. Confidence mask for valid depth regions

Right now the network in [positioning/estimators/network_estimator.py](positioning/estimators/network_estimator.py) sees raw normalized depth; adding geometric priors makes it less sensitive to rough backgrounds and reduces pressure on the model to “discover” basic 3D cues each time.

**4. Train as two tasks: objectness + pose**
1. First head: “is target object present / where likely”
2. Second head: pose only on confident regions/features

This is a major robustness upgrade in real scenes. It avoids forcing a pure pose regressor to solve detection and pose implicitly in one step.

**5. Use teacher-student adaptation with your classical pipeline**
1. Run the classical estimator in [positioning/estimators/algorithm_estimator.py](positioning/estimators/algorithm_estimator.py) on real captures
2. Keep only high-confidence outputs as pseudo-labels
3. Fine-tune the network on these real samples with confidence weighting

This turns your benchmark into a data engine for adaptation, not just a comparator.

**6. Build explicit uncertainty and fallback logic into inference**
1. Predict pose + confidence/uncertainty
2. If uncertainty is high, trigger ICP or classical fallback
3. Return both estimate and trust score

For real deployment this is fundamental. A fast model that knows when it is unsure beats a faster model that is confidently wrong.

**7. Redefine the dataset around “domains,” not just samples**
1. Domain labels: synthetic clean, synthetic randomized, real background composite, real captured
2. Balanced batch sampler across domains
3. Per-domain metrics in validation

This makes generalization measurable and prevents overfitting to whichever generator currently dominates.

**8. Move to protocol-based evaluation, not single loss curves**
1. Pose metrics stratified by clutter level, occlusion level, depth quality
2. Robustness curves: accuracy vs background roughness
3. Failure taxonomy: symmetric flips, translation bias, false lock on clutter

This will reveal whether changes actually improve real-world behavior, not just validation loss.

**9. Introduce shape-family curriculum**
1. Start with broad desktop-like object families for robust geometric priors
2. Then progressively bias training toward blade-like elongated objects
3. Keep a fraction of broad data to prevent specialization collapse

This directly fits your “varied items for generalization” idea while preserving relevance to turbine-blade-like geometry.

**10. Enforce plugin interfaces from day one in v2**
1. Estimator interface: estimate + confidence + debug artifacts
2. Data backend interface: sample scene, sample object, sample background
3. Refinement interface: ICP/post-filter interchangeable
4. Model registry: swap encoders/heads without touching training loop

That keeps v2 clean as it grows and avoids the “messy monolith” problem again.

response.value: You are asking for a practical v2 dataset-generation blueprint that stays modular and manageable, so I’ll quickly inspect the current generation pipeline files and then map your idea into a step-by-step build plan with folder structure, milestones, and what to implement first.

Your direction is solid, and yes, skipping heavy handcrafted depth preprocessing is reasonable if the CNN already performs well. In your case, the biggest gains will come from data realism, clean modular tooling, and consistent geometry conventions.

What you already covered well:
1. Modular camera capture with driver abstraction.
2. Mixing superquadrics with STL objects.
3. Plane fitting for realistic placement.
4. Background-only capture and compositing idea.

What you are still missing (important):
1. Coordinate and unit conventions.
You need one canonical convention for all assets: meters, right-handed frame, forward axis, and camera frame. Most sim-to-real bugs come from hidden convention mismatches.
2. Symmetry metadata per object.
For elongated or near-symmetric shapes, multiple rotations are equivalent. Store symmetry info with each object so training and evaluation do not punish valid equivalent poses.
3. Object quality filtering for STL pool.
Many public STLs are non-watertight, huge/small scale, or weird topology. Add an offline sanitize step before they enter the generation pool.
4. Occlusion and truncation control.
Explicitly generate partial visibility cases, not just clean full-object views.
5. Domain tags in metadata.
Mark each sample as synthetic_only, real_bg_composite, superquadric, stl, occluded, etc. This makes debugging and later ablations much easier.
6. Real camera artifact simulation.
For L515-like depth, add missing-depth holes, edge artifacts, quantization, and depth jitter. This is often more important than shape diversity alone.
7. Train/val split by object identity.
For generalization, keep some object IDs only in validation so you can measure unseen-object performance honestly.

Detailed implementation plan (student-friendly, structured but not heavy)

Phase 1: Lock interfaces and folder layout
1. Keep the three-part split already created in positioning v2/project_layout.md and positioning v2/data_engine/data_engine.py.
2. In data engine, define these submodules:
3. capture for camera background collection
4. assets for STL ingestion and normalization
